lines.trans: Chef, what difference does it make who earns money?
A real restaurant makes good food.
Only Louis's accent will remain in our restaurant.
Because they will kick all of us out of here.
Guys, attention, everyone listen carefully.
Today we have a banquet for an important man.
He is a very important man with big money.
So let us do everything at the highest level.
Did everyone understand me? Come on, brothers, to work!
We are even supposed to help sell ourselves more expensively!
No way, they will not live to see that!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: По каким ещё таким признакам?

examples.text: Мы ещё и поможем продать себя подороже!

examples.text: Лёва, ты ещё хорошо подумай.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Мы ещё и поможем продать себя подороже!

examples.text: Конечно, помогу.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sell', paired with 'продавать'.

examples.text: Хоть продавай теперь наш ресторан.
examples.trans: I might as well sell our restaurant now.

examples.text: Этот человек предложил Нагиеву продать ресторан.
examples.trans: That man offered Nagiyev to sell the restaurant.

examples.text: Он хочет продать наш ресторан.

examples.text: Мы ещё и поможем продать себя подороже!

examples.text: Если не можешь запомнить, покупай себе блокнот.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рогой').

examples.text: Это дорогая одежда.

examples.text: Дорогая, я дома!

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

дождаться.gloss: to wait for, to live to see

meanings.en: to wait until something happens, to get by waiting (+ genitive)
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ждаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait for, to live to see', paired with 'дожидаться'.

examples.text: Я дождусь ответа.
examples.trans: I will wait for an answer.

examples.text: Я всё равно дождусь твоего ответа!
examples.trans: I will wait for your answer anyway!

examples.text: Я готов спокойно дождаться решения суда.
examples.trans: I am ready to wait calmly for the court decision.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'to the guest' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас обслуживание гостей на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Our guest service is at the highest level.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, к вам пришёл гость.
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, a guest has come to see you.

examples.text: Мы этому гостю такой банкет сегодня устроим!
examples.trans: We will throw such a banquet for this guest today!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, what sort', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.en: to arrange, organize, set up an event or scheme
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'строить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will arrange / throw', paired with 'устраивать'.

examples.text: Мы этому гостю такой банкет сегодня устроим!
examples.trans: We will throw such a banquet for this guest today!

examples.trans: I will arrange everything at the highest level.

examples.text: Они устроили праздник для друзей.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Он всегда точно знает, что делать.

examples.text: По признакам всё точно сходится.

examples.text: Они этого точно не дождутся!
